In my [portfolio project](/case-studies/portfolio), I've been exploring how RAG can create more grounded and precise AI interactions by dynamically retrieving and integrating relevant context.

question: Explore your product management philosophy
old_response:
My product management philosophy centers on three core principles: user-centricity, strategic pragmatism, and continuous learning.

First, I believe products must solve real user problems, not just implement features. In my [RatedPower topography tool](/case-studies/ratedpower-topography), we deliberately chose "good enough" accuracy that matched user needs instead of over-engineering. Our customer success team was critical in understanding genuine pain points, which guided our development.

Second, I prioritize strategic trade-offs that balance mission and business sustainability. At [Ecometro](/case-studies/ecometro-product-strategy), I demonstrated this by convincing the board to initially target enterprise clients—not as a departure from their sustainability mission, but as a strategic path to eventually democratize their technology. Business model and social impact aren't opposing forces, but interconnected strategies.

Lastly, I embrace continuous learning through phased releases, close partner collaboration, and a willingness to challenge existing assumptions. My work consistently shows that products evolve through direct user feedback, not theoretical perfection. By building adaptable architectures and maintaining close communication with users and stakeholders, we can create solutions that genuinely transform industries.

new_response:

For me, this means staying ahead of technological shifts while maintaining a laser focus on practical outcomes. A perfect example is my approach to AI product development, where I emphasize understanding both capabilities and limitations. As I discussed in [my thoughts on AI and Product Management](/case-studies/portfolio-rag-chatbot), the best products aren't about chasing the latest trend, but thoughtfully integrating new technologies where they genuinely improve user experience.

I also believe in rigorous validation and phased learning. In my [RatedPower topography tool](/case-studies/ratedpower-topography) project, we demonstrated this by releasing in three phases, which allowed us to continuously validate with real users and build confidence in our approach. question: How do you work?
old_response:
I approach product management and technical development with a structured, collaborative, and iterative methodology. My workflow centers on three key principles: evidence-based decision making, continuous validation, and cross-functional teamwork.

Take my work at [RatedPower](/case-studies/ratedpower-topography) as an example. I always prioritize shipping in phases, validating with real users between releases. This allows me to de-risk complex features and ensure we're building something that genuinely solves customer problems. I embed myself directly in the feedback loop, maintaining close relationships with Customer Success teams and a core group of power users who help me validate ideas before full implementation.

In my recent [portfolio website project](/case-studies/portfolio), I took this approach even further by using an advanced agent-based development process called "Ralph Wiggum". This autonomous workflow allows specialized AI agents to work through implementation plans, run tests, and iterate independently, with human review happening at key phase completions. This dramatically accelerated development while maintaining strict quality gates like test-driven development (TDD) and comprehensive code reviews.

As I mentioned in my background, if I believe a client or colleague has a challenge, I'm committed to fully understanding the context before developing a solution. This approach has been critical in my work across different projects like [RatedPower](/case-studies/ratedpower-topography), where I developed complex topography tools by continuously validating with users and making strategic decisions.
